# Lacuna v0.7.0

Lacuna `v0.7.0` is the portable-evidence milestone. An immutable audit can now become a deterministic,
checksummed `.lacuna` archive whose structure and artifact integrity are independently verifiable
without extraction, rendering, plugin activation, or code execution.

## Highlights

- `AuditReport.bundle(...)` and `lacuna.create_bundle(...)` package canonical JSON,
  escaped Markdown/self-contained HTML, resolved configuration and environment summaries, and
  optional named `AnalysisResult`, provenance, and invocation evidence.
- `lacuna.verify_bundle(...)` and `lacuna bundle verify` validate canonical paths, regular
  non-executable file types, bounded sizes/counts, exact member set, canonical ZIP/JSON encoding,
  report identity, artifact-set SHA-256, and every member SHA-256.
- A published bundle-manifest v1 JSON Schema is available in the repository and installed wheel,
  with a persisted migration fixture and a frozen additive core `0.7.x` API contract.
- Supplemental metadata redacts credential-shaped keys, URL credentials/query/fragment, and
  machine-specific absolute paths while retaining a value-free redaction log. Canonical reports and
  named evidence fail closed instead of being silently rewritten.
- Markdown reports now escape source-derived HTML metacharacters so hostile finding text remains
  text in downstream renderers.
- `lacuna signal --bundle study.lacuna` creates a report and portable archive in one file workflow;
  clean-wheel release tests exercise creation, verification, and the packaged schema.

## Reproducibility and trust boundary

Bundle v1 claims **identifiable** reproducibility only: declared artifact bytes are internally
consistent with their manifest. It does not claim authorship, input availability, recomputability,
numerical reproduction, or cross-machine bitwise reproduction. SHA-256 is not a signature; use the
GitHub provenance attached to release distributions or another trusted channel to establish origin.

The writer adds no source datasets, arbitrary files, lockfiles, credentials, environment variables,
plugins, pickle, or executable content automatically. The verifier enforces 256 members, 16 MiB per
member, 64 MiB total, and a 64 MiB archive, and rejects traversal, drive paths, duplicates, links,
executable modes, encryption, compression, comments, extra members, and noncanonical encodings.

## Compatibility and distribution

Core `0.7.0` is additive over every published `0.1.x` through `0.6.x` Python contract. The embedded
audit result remains schema version 1; bundle layout compatibility is selected independently by
`bundle_version=1`.

The separately versioned options extension advances to `0.1.1` only to expand its compatible core
range to `lacuna>=0.5,<0.8`; its exact `0.1.x` source and public API are unchanged and re-run through
the property, coverage, packaging, and joint-install gates.

This release is distributed through GitHub because the `lacuna` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated
project. The release contains four target-smoke-tested CPython 3.11 stable-ABI core wheels, one
universal options wheel, both source distributions, `SHA256SUMS`, and GitHub provenance for every
distribution.

The v1 readiness ledger records the remaining work candidly: cross-phase standardized audit is the
candidate `0.8` milestone, migration/operational hardening is the candidate `0.9` milestone, and
`1.0.0` still requires independent users applying Lacuna to real research stacks.
